Diagnostic Plots of the Parametric Distributions

Source: R/plot_distribution_diagnostics.R
plot_distribution_diagnostics.Rd

Plots transformations of the Kaplan-Meier estimate (or of the smoothed empirical hazard) of each arm that are straight lines when the data follow a distribution:

  • "weibull": log(-log(S(t))) against log(t), straight for the Weibull (slope = shape; slope 1 for the exponential). Parallel lines also indicate proportional hazards, so this is the log cumulative hazard plot of the proportional hazards assessment.

  • "loglogistic": log((1 - S(t)) / S(t)) against log(t), straight for the log-logistic.

  • "lognormal": qnorm(1 - S(t)) against log(t), straight for the lognormal.

  • "gompertz": log(h(t)) of the smoothed empirical hazard against t, straight for the Gompertz.

The Kaplan-Meier estimate is used at the event times where it is strictly between 0 and 1. With regression = TRUE the least-squares line of each arm is added (dashed).

Usage

plot_distribution_diagnostics(
  data,
  which = c("weibull", "loglogistic", "lognormal", "gompertz"),
  regression = TRUE,
  time_unit = c("months", "days", "weeks", "years"),
  legend_position = c("bottom", "right", "top", "left", "none"),
  colours = NULL,
  linetypes = NULL,
  text_sizes = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame returned by processing_dataset.

which

Character vector with the plots, a subset of c("weibull", "loglogistic", "lognormal", "gompertz") (the default, all four).

regression

Logical; TRUE (the default) adds the least-squares line of each arm.

time_unit

Time unit of the data: "months" (the default), "days", "weeks" or "years".

legend_position

Position of the legend: "bottom" (the default), "right", "top", "left" or "none".

colours

NULL (the default colours of the arms, the same in all plots) or colours of the arms: a vector named by arm, for some or all of the arms, or an unnamed vector with one colour per arm, in the order of the arms.

linetypes

NULL (the default, solid lines) or line types of the curves of the arms, given as for colours (see plot_km); the least-squares lines are dashed.

text_sizes

NULL (the default) or a named vector of font sizes in points, with some or all of the names "title" (titles of the plot and of its panels), "axis_title", "axis_text", "legend" and "risk_table" (numbers at risk and names of the arms below the plot; the title of the table is 1.125 times as large). The texts not named keep their default sizes: 14 points for the axis titles, 16.8 for the title of a plot, and 11.2 for the titles of panels, the axis text, the legend and the numbers at risk.

Value

A ggplot object for a single plot, otherwise a patchwork object with the plots in the order of which, two per row, and one legend.

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
plot_distribution_diagnostics(dat)

plot_distribution_diagnostics(dat, which = "weibull")
